title: External objects, Salesforce Connect, and data virtualization

objectives: Define Salesforce Connect as the adapter framework that surfaces external data as external objects without storing those rows.
Use indirect lookup when the remote key is not a Salesforce Id.
Choose virtualization versus batch copy using INT-001 how much/how fast and INT-003 styles.
Authenticate Connect callouts with named credentials (INT-004), not secrets in Apex.
diagnostic_question: ERP bins must appear on Account without a Salesforce bin table, keys are ERP customer numbers, and reports also need last night's snapshot. What is Connect vs a copy, and which lookup type?
definition: Data virtualization lets Salesforce access external data in real time without persisting a copy to reconcile. Salesforce Connect provides adapters (for example OData) that map remote tables to external objects—schema projections that hold no stored rows. Indirect lookup relates an external child to a Salesforce parent using a unique External Id field, not a Salesforce Id. ([Data Virtualization](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/data-virtualization.html); [Indirect lookup](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.external_object_indirect_lookup_relationships.htm); [Integration Patterns](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/integration-patterns))
why_it_matters: Teams that copy nightly and call it Connect still reconcile. Teams that virtualize huge interactive reports without measuring remote latency create timeouts. Interviewers want projection vs copy and indirect lookup.
sixty_second_explanation: Imagine a telescope aimed at a warehouse you do not own. Salesforce Connect is the telescope mount. External objects are the labeled views in the eyepiece—not crates in your warehouse. Indirect lookup is matching their stenciled customer number to your unique External Id, because they do not paint Salesforce Ids on the crates. If you also keep a snapshot fridge, say so—that is a copy, not the telescope.
deeper_explanation: Architects page: Connect translates SOQL to the remote query language, authenticates, maps types. External objects behave like platform objects in many UI/API ways but store no data. Live callouts happen when users query. ([Virtualization](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/data-virtualization.html))

Indirect lookup: child external object to parent standard/custom object by matching a unique External Id on the parent. Direct Salesforce Ids will not exist on the remote row. ([Indirect lookup Help](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.external_object_indirect_lookup_relationships.htm))

Editions: Connect is in Developer Edition and extra cost in Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited as documented on that Help page. Adapter limits changed on Hyperforce in recent releases—Needs verification of current General Limits for Salesforce Connect; do not quote old row caps as eternal.
Named credentials authenticate adapters (INT-004). Formula/validation/automation support on external objects is feature-specific—Needs verification rather than repeating old blog restrictions as law.

mental_model.analogy: A telescope on a warehouse you do not own: Connect is the mount, external objects are eyepiece views, indirect lookup matches stenciled numbers, a snapshot fridge is a separate copy.
useful_mapping: external object → eyepiece view (__x), no crates stored
indirect lookup → stencil number vs your External Id
named credential → badge to enter their warehouse
batch copy → your own fridge to reconcile
live SOQL on __x → looking now, remote may be down
where_it_breaks: Telescope shows errors if the warehouse is dark—no pretty cached picture unless you add a copy.
Report/offline needs may force a snapshot (INT-003 two-style design).
License and adapter limits are not magnification numbers to invent.

claims.claim: Data Virtualization: Salesforce accesses external data in real time without persisting a copy that must then be reconciled.
Salesforce Connect maps remote data to external objects. External objects are a schema projection and hold no stored data; queries cause real-time callouts.
Indirect lookup links a child external object to a parent Salesforce object by matching a unique External Id field because remote rows do not carry Salesforce Ids.
Salesforce Connect edition availability is documented as Developer Edition and extra cost in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited on the indirect-lookup Help article.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Connect virtualizes remote tables as external objects with no stored rows. Indirect lookup matches their key to our unique External Id. A snapshot table is a copy, not Connect.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I only virtualize when INT-001 how fast is live-look and we refuse reconciliation. Named credentials authenticate. If finance needs yesterday's numbers offline, I add an explicit batch copy. I will not quote expired row limits. Remote downtime is an error, not a cache, unless we built one.

when_to_use: When you need external objects, Salesforce Connect, and data virtualization instead of a stored copy.
When remote keys are not Salesforce Ids and indirect lookup to a unique External Id is required.
When how fast is live page access and how much per user query is a modest related list, not a million-row extract.
When named credentials should authenticate the Connect adapter (INT-004).
When an interview asks projection versus nightly reconcile.
when_not_to_use: Do not virtualize a million-row interactive report without measuring the remote system (use batch extracts/Bulk).
Do not call a custom-object copy Salesforce Connect.
Do not invent Connect row limits from old blogs.
Do not skip External Id uniqueness for indirect lookup.
Do not point Connect at production ERP from this lesson.

interview_questions.question: Explain external objects, Salesforce Connect, and data virtualization.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Connect adapters project remote tables as __x objects with no stored rows. That is the virtualization pattern. Indirect lookup maps non-Salesforce keys.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I contrast a nightly __c copy. Auth is named credentials. Limits and formulas Needs verification. Remote downtime is live failure.
interview_questions.example: ERP bins on Account plus optional snapshot.

interview_questions.question: When is Connect the wrong tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Huge extracts, offline-mandated reports, or when a copy is already the system of record in Salesforce.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: How much and how fast from INT-001 still apply. Salesforce Connect virtualization is live per access, not a warehouse dump. For a two-million-row finance CSV I use batch or Bulk, and I will not fake a Connect SKU as if it stored those rows.
interview_questions.example: Finance needs a CSV of two million ERP rows for a closed-period audit, so we copy, not Connect.

interview_questions.question: ERP customer number, Salesforce Accounts, live orders related list.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unique External Id on Account, Connect orders __x, indirect lookup.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: ERP has a customer number, not a Salesforce Account Id, so I use an indirect lookup from the external order object to Account.CustNum__c as a unique External Id. I test matching in a sandbox and put a named credential on the Salesforce Connect source, not a hard-coded password.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CustNum__c unique External Id plus LAB_ERP_Order__x related list on Account.

interview_questions.question: They already nightly-load orders and want Connect 'too'.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Two styles: keep the copy for reports; add __x only if live extra columns are worth the latency. Do not double-name them Connect.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: They already nightly-load orders, so adding Connect as well creates two truths. Reconciliation (INT-010) applies to the stored copy. The virtualization path has no persisted rows to cycle-count. I pick one pattern unless a documented hybrid is required.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Order__c snapshot plus LAB_Order__x live status.

interview_questions.question: The external-object related list is empty. What do you check first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: External Id mismatch, user perms, adapter filter, remote empty—not a missing Salesforce row store.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare stencil numbers on both sides of the indirect lookup, then check named-credential HTTP 401 versus a 200 with zero rows. Trailing spaces on ERP customer numbers are common. I do not Data Loader into an __x object expecting Salesforce storage.
interview_questions.example: ERP CustNum has a trailing space that does not match Account.CustNum__c in Salesforce.

interview_questions.question: Page times out on the related list.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Remote latency or too-wide query. Narrow filters or stop using Connect for that list; consider copy for that UX.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not invent timeout defaults. I capture debug of the Connect callout. Huge unfiltered __x lists are a how-much fail.
interview_questions.example: Related list without a where clause on a large OData set.

interview_questions.question: Indirect vs external lookup vs lookup—what do you actually say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Indirect: external child, Salesforce parent, External Id match. I will not invent the other types' field lists; I open Help if they want external parent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The assigned Help article is indirect lookup. I admit neighboring relationship types exist and I will not bluff column names.
interview_questions.example: Account is the Salesforce parent; ERP order is the external-object child via indirect lookup.

interview_questions.question: Teach the telescope analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Connect mount, __x eyepiece, stencil numbers, snapshot fridge. It breaks when the warehouse is dark or when I invent magnification limits.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The telescope maps Salesforce Connect to a live view of the remote warehouse; external objects are the eyepiece, not stored crates. It breaks for offline reports, which need a copy, and for invented adapter SLAs. Named credentials are the badge at the gate, not the lens type. Live ERP errors surface in Salesforce UX instead of a stale snapshot.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard bins live plus finance snapshot.
